messages:
maria: CI went red on windows-integ after I regenerated the poetry.lock this morning — failing test looks like networking timeouts coming from the Azure SDK. Anyone seen this pattern?

jamal: which job and test? can you paste the failing snippet?

maria: job=py-integration-windows-3.9, test=tests/service/test_httpclient.py::test_parallel_requests. Repro locally inside the windows CI image. Relevant tail of the log:```
E   requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='vault.local', port=443): Read timed out.
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
E   azure.core.exceptions.ServiceRequestError: Failed to send request: ReadTimeout
```

aisha: hmmm. any recent deps that could affect transport? urllib3, requests, or azure-core/identity?

maria: I regen'd lock after merging the constraints update from #452. lock diff shows urllib3 bumped 1.26.14 -> 2.0.0 and httpx -> 0.24.x, also azure-core stayed at 1.25.x but wheel pulled in urllib3 2.0 transitively via some dep.

ben: azure-core (1.x) historically expects urllib3 <2.0 in some codepaths. Could be an incompat. try pinning urllib3<2 in the env to confirm.

jamal: can you run a quick local venv with constraints pin to verify? if that fixes it, we need to bisect the lock regen to find which transitive bump introduced the 2.x urllib3.

maria: doing that now. quick patch: `poetry add --lock --constraint "urllib3<2"` then rerun tests.

ci-bot: Build triggered: py-integration-windows-3.9 (rerun) by maria

maria: ok test rerun passed locally with urllib3 pinned. So this is reproducible and likely a transitive compatibility issue.

aisha: thanks. can you run `scripts/lock-bisect.py --start-rev HEAD~8 --end-rev HEAD --job windows-integ --test tests/service/test_httpclient.py::test_parallel_requests` and paste the output? that will point to the offending commit in the lock regen chain.

maria: started bisect, output:```
bisect: trying lock at rev=commit-ef1a (2024-11-02) -> tests fail
bisect: trying lock at rev=commit-d4b2 (2024-10-29) -> tests pass
=> first bad lock rev=commit-ef1a
lock diff for commit-ef1a: urllib3 1.26.14 -> 2.0.0 (via transitive bump from package 'some-http-client')
```

ben: nice. so the immediate cause is a transitive bump to urllib3 2.0. two options: 1) add an explicit constraint urllib3<2 in our constraints/pyproject to keep lock regen safe, or 2) update azure-core and any other libs to versions that are known-compatible with urllib3 2.x.

jamal: check whether updating azure-core to the next minor removes the issue. but that might be a larger change. I'm +1 for a short-term constraint pin (umbrella constraints) and a ticket to upgrade libs and run full evals.

maria: created an issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2345 — notes: "Windows integ failures after lock regen due to urllib3 2.0 transitive bump; temporary constraint urllib3<2; evaluate dependency upgrades". Added the bisect output and failing logs.

aisha: loop in security/platform to verify no CVE/approved exception needed for temporary pin. Also add a console rollout to ensure Dedicated customers don't pick up a bad private lock when they import.

ben: i'll open a PR with the constraint pin and a changelog entry explaining the short-term fix + plan to upgrade azure libs. assign to maria for verification.

maria: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/789 — includes `constraints/urllib3: "<2"` and a short test run. tagging @jamal for review.

jamal: reviewing now. after merge, let's re-run full CI on windows-integ and the mac/linux matrices.

ci-bot: Job py-integration-windows-3.9 queued (after constraints PR merge).

maria: thanks team — will monitor. filing follow-up to remove the pin after we've verified upstream libs are compatible. :thumbsup:
